chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said:

Tablets came out to us from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Baṣrah, and written in them across was: “My covenant is to my eldest son: so-and-so is to be given such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such; and so-and-so is not to be given until I come, or Allah, Mighty and Majestic, decrees death upon me.”
Surely Allah does whatever He wills.

key_terms.أَكْبَرِ وُلْدِي: my eldest son, indicating primary filial succession in this instruction
key_terms.لَا يُعْطَى: is not to be given, indicating suspension or withholding
key_terms.يُعْطَى: is to be given, referring to designated disbursement

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام’s written covenant to his eldest son indicate?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written directive from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Baṣrah, assigning responsibility to his eldest son regarding designated distributions and withholding one case pending his return or death. It also closes with an affirmation of Allah’s absolute will, reflecting both orderly succession and divine decree.
